name: Lausanne, Lavaux and Montreux
tagline: Terraced vineyards tumbling to Lake Geneva, a hilltop Gothic cathedral, a lakeside fairy-tale castle and the Riviera of Montreux.
highlight: Walking the Lavaux terraces with a glass of chasselas, the lake shining below and the Alps across the water.
shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed stretch of vineyard terraces on Lake Geneva, with hillside Lausanne, its cathedral and Ouchy waterfront, the Château de Chillon at Montreux and lake steamers.
metaDescription: A Lausanne and Lavaux travel guide: UNESCO vineyard terraces, wine tasting, Lausanne Cathedral, Ouchy, Château de Chillon at Montreux, St-Saphorin, lake boats, where to stay and a two-day plan.
knownFor: Lavaux vineyards, Chillon Castle, Lausanne Cathedral, lake views
goodFor: Wine, walking, lake cruises, castles, slow travel

image.alt: The terraced vineyards of Lavaux above Lake Geneva

intro: The northern shore of Lake Geneva, in the canton of Vaud, is Switzerland's sunny south-facing riviera. Between Lausanne and Montreux, steep terraces of vines, built by monks in the 12th century, tumble to the water. This landscape, Lavaux, about 30 km long, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and its villages, such as Saint-Saphorin and Cully, produce fine white wines from the chasselas grape.

Lausanne, the region's main city, is built on three hills above the lake. Its Gothic cathedral is one of the finest in Switzerland, the old town is steep and cobbled, and the waterfront district of Ouchy has promenades, parks and paddle steamers. Lausanne is also the Olympic capital, home to the International Olympic Committee and a strong Olympic museum. At the other end of the shore, Montreux, known for its jazz festival and Freddie Mercury statue, has a palm-lined lakeside promenade and, just beyond, the Château de Chillon, a medieval castle on a rock in the water.

The best way to see it is on foot and by train, using the regional trains that run along the lakeshore, and the boats that link the towns. A day can be spent walking between vineyards, tasting wine at family cellars and sipping a glass with lake views. Two days lets you add Lausanne and Chillon.

whyVisit.intro: This is Switzerland's wine country, with lake views instead of mountains at every turn.

points.title: A fairy-tale castle
points.text: Château de Chillon on the water.

attractionsIntro: The sights are along the lakeshore, linked by train and boat.

attractions.name: Lavaux vineyard terraces

image.file: File:View on St-Saphorin at Lac Geneva.jpg
image.alt: The village of Saint-Saphorin among Lavaux vineyards, above Lake Geneva

attractions.text: A 30-km stretch of terraces, with walking paths between Lausanne and Vevey and wine cellars in stone villages.
attractions.tip: Walk from Lutry or Cully to St-Saphorin.

attractions.name: Château de Chillon

image.alt: Château de Chillon on a rock at the edge of Lake Geneva

attractions.text: A medieval island castle on Lake Geneva, once home to the Counts of Savoy, and the subject of Lord Byron's poem The Prisoner of Chillon.
attractions.tip: Go early to avoid tour buses.

attractions.name: Lausanne Cathedral

image.alt: Lausanne Cathedral rising above the old town

attractions.text: A Gothic cathedral consecrated in 1275, with a tower whose night watchman still calls out the hours.

attractions.name: Ouchy

image.file: File:CGN Ville-de-Genève and SS Montreux in Lausanne-Ouchy (2015).jpg
image.alt: Paddle steamers at the Ouchy harbour in Lausanne

attractions.text: Lausanne's waterfront, with paddle steamers, promenades, cafés and the Olympic Museum.
attractions.tip: Take the metro down from the centre.

attractions.name: Montreux promenade
attractions.text: A lakeside path lined with palms and flowers, with a statue of Freddie Mercury.
attractions.tip: Walk to Chillon along the lake.

attractions.name: Olympic Museum
attractions.text: A museum on the history of the Games, with a park.

thingsToDoIntro: Wine, walks and boats fill the days.

thingsToDo.title: Walk through the vines
thingsToDo.text: Follow the marked paths between villages.

thingsToDo.title: Cruise the lake
thingsToDo.tip: Included in the Swiss Travel Pass.

thingsToDo.title: Ride the Lavaux Express
thingsToDo.text: A small tourist train through the vineyards.

thingsToDo.title: Take the GoldenPass to Montreux
thingsToDo.text: A scenic railway from the mountains.

foodIntro: Vaud food is French-Swiss, and goes with white wine.

foods.name: Chasselas wine
foods.text: A light white wine from Lavaux.

accommodation.intro: Stay in Lausanne for the city or in Vevey or Montreux for the lake.

gettingThere.intro: The lakeshore is on the main rail line.

bestTime.headline: May–October
bestTime.summary: The lakeshore has a mild climate, with warm summers and grape harvests in autumn.

seasons.text: Warm, though vineyard walks can be hot.
Quiet, with Christmas markets in Montreux.

bestTime.avoid: Midday heat on the terraces in July and August.

itinerary.title: Two days on Lake Geneva
itinerary.intro: Vineyards on the first day, and the cathedral and castle on the second.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you plan.
tips: Walk downhill from Chexbres to save effort.

faq.q: How many days do you need?

faq.a: UNESCO vineyard terraces and chasselas wine.

faq.q: How do I get to Chillon?
faq.a: Train to Veytaux-Chillon or a bus from Montreux.

faq.q: Can I do it as a day trip from Geneva?

faq.a: Yes, for the cathedral and lakefront.
